# Results — Study 930 (When-Issued Window) on the real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). A hand-compiled table of 26
liquid US spin-offs (2012–2025) is cut into three windows: the **parent** from the day
after the separation was announced to the last close before the child trades regular way;
the **child** over its first 5 / 10 / 21 regular-way sessions; and the **parent + child**
combination held 21 sessions from the first regular-way close. Every window is an alpha
versus **SPY** — long the asset, short the index, **one dollar against one dollar** — so it
is cash-neutral by construction and excess-of-cash *is* the spread. Daily **total-return**
closes (`yfinance`, `auto_adjust=True`). Frictions: **10 bps one-way × NAV** on the spin-off
side (a round trip each way = 2×), 1 bp on SPY, and **40 bp/yr borrow on the short SPY leg**.
One execution lag throughout: the parent is bought at the close of the session *after* the
announcement, the child at the close of its *first* regular-way session (so the day-one pop
is excluded). As-of **2026-06-30**.*

## Data stamp

| Legs | Window | Events | Tickers | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|--:|---|
| 26 parents + 26 children + SPY + BIL | distributions 2012-05-01 → 2025-02-24 | 26 (≈2.0/yr) | 52 | Fingerprint `e78725a81ebe` |

The stamp is taken over 2011-01-01 → as-of, not over the whole frame: the desk cache is
shared, and another study re-fetching SPY or BIL with a different start date would otherwise
move the fingerprint without changing a single number in this file.

Four further spin-offs belong in the table on the merits but Yahoo no longer serves their
**child** because it was acquired and delisted (**AAN**, **VSCO**, **ZIMV**, **KLG**). They
are recorded in `data.DELISTED_EVENTS` so the hole is visible; note it removes outcomes of
*both* signs (WK Kellogg and ZimVie were taken out at a premium).

## Which number is the headline, and why

The child leg's raw alpha is **negative**. Charging a long position's round-trip costs to a
negative number makes it *more* negative — the wrong direction for a headline — so the
stated effect size below is the **gross** abnormal return, and the net-of-frictions long
figure is quoted beside it only to show that frictions are not what create the effect. The
costed number that decides tradability is the mirror trade (short the child), where the
frictions land on the side you would actually pay them.

**Unit beta is an assumption.** No beta is estimated anywhere: every leg is a 1:1 dollar
spread. A freshly spun child is typically higher-beta and smaller-cap than SPY; over five
sessions that error is second-order next to the idiosyncratic move, and the swap to IWM and
MDY below is the check on it. This is a dollar hedge, not a risk-model alpha.

## The three legs — alpha vs SPY

Gross (the effect), with the net-of-frictions long version in the last column.

| Leg | n | Mean (gross) | Median | Hit rate [Wilson] | *t* | HAC *t* | 95% bootstrap CI | Net long |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Parent, announcement → distribution | 26 | −1.45% | −2.28% | 0.42 [0.26, 0.61] | −0.26 | −0.47 | [−11.43, +9.47]% | −2.10% (*t* = −0.38) |
| **Child, first 5 sessions** | 26 | **−4.54%** | −4.36% | **0.31** [0.17, 0.50] | **−2.73** | **−3.02** | **[−7.67, −1.42]%** | −4.77% (*t* = −2.87) |
| Child, first 10 sessions | 26 | −3.47% | −3.09% | 0.31 [0.17, 0.50] | −1.61 | −2.20 | [−7.61, +0.63]% | −3.71% (*t* = −1.71) |
| Child, first 21 sessions | 26 | −1.02% | −1.87% | 0.46 [0.29, 0.65] | −0.41 | −0.58 | [−5.75, +3.73]% | −1.27% (*t* = −0.51) |
| Parent + child, first 21 sessions | 26 | +1.88% | +2.80% | 0.62 [0.43, 0.78] | +1.28 | +1.44 | [−1.02, +4.69]% | +1.62% (*t* = +1.10) |

The one leg that clears |*t*| ≥ 2 clears it **gross and net**, and it clears it with the
**opposite sign** to the folklore: the child does not snap back off forced selling, it
keeps falling. Per-trade dispersion is **8.5 pp**, so the mean is a thin edge over a wide
distribution — 8 of 26 events are positive.

## Five legs were pre-specified, so the family is priced

Quoting the best of five as though it were the only one tested is the sin this desk audits
for. `strategy.family_wise_p` runs a Westfall-Young max-|*t*| bootstrap: events are
resampled jointly across all five legs after each is centred on its own mean, so the null is
imposed while the (strong) cross-leg correlation is preserved — child +5, +10 and +21 share
their first five sessions, and Bonferroni would over-punish exactly because of that.

| Leg | parent | **child +5** | child +10 | child +21 | parent+child |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| *t* (gross) | −0.26 | **−2.73** | −1.61 | −0.41 | +1.28 |

Strongest leg, single-test bootstrap *p* = **0.0088**; **family-wise *p* over the five legs
= 0.0452**. It survives, and it survives *narrowly*: the effect is real at the 5% level
after paying for all five looks, not comfortably so. Anyone reading this as a strong result
is reading it wrong.

## Robustness on the 5-session child leg

Gross, since that is the headline; the net-long figures are in brackets and are uniformly
a shade stronger, which is the point.

| Check | Result (gross) |
|---|---|
| Era cut (split 2020-01-01, by distribution) | early n = 6: **−3.77%** (*t* = −2.91) · late n = 20: **−4.77%** (*t* = −2.23) — negative in **both** [net: −4.00%/−4.99%, *t* = −3.09/−2.33] |
| Benchmark swap (children are small/mid, SPY is not) | vs SPY −4.54% (*t* = −2.73) · vs **IWM** −4.41% (*t* = −2.48) · vs **MDY** −4.64% (*t* = −2.62) |
| Leave-one-out (jackknife) | *t* ranges **−3.36 … −2.44** — no single event carries it [net: −3.51 … −2.58] |
| De-clustered (one event per calendar quarter) | n = 19, **−5.09%** (*t* = −2.88) — the 2023-10 cluster is not the story [net: −5.32%, *t* = −3.01] |
| Cost sweep (charged to the *long* version) | 0 bps −4.56% (*t* = −2.74) · 25 bps −5.07% (*t* = −3.05) · 50 bps −5.57% (*t* = −3.35). Costs make a *negative* alpha worse, so they cannot be what creates it — and that is also why they are not in the headline. |
| SPY borrow sweep | 0 / 40 / 100 bp/yr moves the mean by 2 bp — immaterial at a 5-session horizon |

## Proxy sweeps — the three non-tape inputs

Every date and ratio in the event table is an **assumption compiled from the public record**,
not something measured off the tape. Each is swept (on the net column, as built).

| Proxy | Sweep | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| **Announcement date** (parent leg) | −5 / −2 / 0 / +2 / +5 sessions | −3.78% → −0.89%; *t* never leaves [−0.67, −0.15]. The parent leg is null at every setting, so nothing hangs on the date. |
| **First regular-way session** (child leg) | −3 / −1 / 0 / +1 / +3 sessions | **−6.85% / −7.76% / −4.77% / −3.31% / +2.24%** (*t* = −2.74 / −3.78 / −2.87 / −1.76 / **+1.62**). This is the load-bearing assumption: anchoring *earlier* (inside the when-issued tail) makes the effect stronger, anchoring three sessions *late* **flips the sign**. Note *n* drops to 24 at the negative shifts, so those two columns are not the same sample. |
| **Distribution ratio** (combined leg) | ×0.5 / ×1 / ×2 / equal weight | +1.75% / +1.62% / +1.41% / +0.37%; *t* ≤ +1.19 throughout. The combined leg is null under every weighting. |

### Is each anchor on the right side of the transition?

Checked in `verify.py` rather than asserted. **25 of 26** stated regular-way dates are
themselves a session on the child's Yahoo series; the exception is **VLTO**, which Yahoo does
not serve on 2023-10-02 or 10-03, so the loader snaps it forward to 10-04 (three sessions
late — which, given the trough at +3, makes that event *conservative*, not flattering).
**24 of 26** children have a genuine when-issued tail of **3–15 sessions** before the anchor,
which is the evidence that the anchor is not set too early; the two without one (**ABBV**,
**VLTO**) simply have no pre-anchor data on Yahoo. The regular-way sweep above is therefore
less a fragility than a *description*: the effect lives in a window three to five sessions
wide, so the anchor has to be right to the session — and it is the one input that would
overturn the result if it were systematically wrong.

|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|

| median | −1.75% | +1.78% | 0.00% | −1.33% | −4.24% | −5.16% | −4.36% | −3.09% | −1.87% |

(The −3 mean and median disagree in sign — one event's when-issued run-up carries that
column. Read the median.)

The horizon grid (gross): +1d −1.18% (*t* = −0.70), +2d −3.72% (*t* = −2.35), **+3d −5.91%
(*t* = −3.65, HAC −4.49, only 3 of 26 events positive)**, +5d −4.54%, +10d −3.47%,
+21d −1.02%, **+63d −0.74% (*t* = −0.19)** — a sharp trough at three sessions that has
substantially filled back in by a month and is entirely gone by a quarter. Those grid
points beyond 5 / 10 / 21 were searched *after* seeing the data, are **not** in the
family-wise test above, and carry an unpriced multiple-comparison penalty; they are here
for the shape, never for the stamp.

## The trade that actually harvests it — short the child, 5 sessions

A negative alpha pays only if the short is financeable, and a freshly distributed spin-off
is the textbook hard-to-borrow name. The borrow rate is a pure **ASSUMPTION** and is swept.
No short rebate is credited on the cash collateral, which is conservative at 2010s rates.

| Child borrow | Mean | *t* | Hit rate [Wilson] | 95% CI |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 %/yr (fantasy) | +4.32% | +2.60 | 0.65 [0.46, 0.81] | [+1.20, +7.45]% |
| 5 %/yr | +4.22% | +2.54 | 0.65 | [+1.10, +7.35]% |
| 25 %/yr | +3.82% | +2.30 | 0.65 | [+0.70, +6.95]% |
| 50 %/yr | +3.33% | +2.00 | 0.62 [0.43, 0.78] | [+0.20, +6.46]% |
| **100 %/yr** | **+2.33%** | **+1.40** | 0.62 | **[−0.79, +5.46]%** — CI includes zero |

Costs are already inside those figures (10 bps one-way each side, round trip both legs).

## The daily hedged sleeve

Equal-weight the children currently inside their window, short SPY against them, cost and
borrow everything daily. The calendar is the **study's own window** (first distribution to
last exit), not whatever pre-history the shared cache happens to hold for SPY — otherwise
the duty cycle would be a fact about parquet files rather than about the strategy.

| Window | Active days | Spread | HAC *t* | Block-bootstrap CI |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5 sessions | 118 of 3,228 (3.7%) | −75.9 bps/day | −1.84 | [−133.6, −9.8] bps |
| 10 sessions | 231 of 3,233 (7.1%) | −27.2 bps/day | −1.05 | [−72.6, +16.5] bps |
| 21 sessions | 453 of 3,244 (14.0%) | −4.2 bps/day | −0.27 | [−32.8, +24.8] bps |

The daily HAC *t* is weaker than the event-level *t* because 26 events give only 118 active
days and they arrive in clusters; the block-bootstrap CI on the 5-day sleeve still excludes
zero. The sleeve is idle ~96% of even its own window — that is a **capacity** statement about
two events a year, not evidence for or against the effect, and it is why no fund-level
Sharpe is quoted here.

## Synthetic control (machinery proof only — never supports the stamp)

On a *planted* world (a real announcement-to-distribution parent run-up and a real
+5.25% child drift over 21 regular-way sessions) the identical estimator recovers
parent **+21.72%** (*t* = +2.60) and child **+6.63%** (*t* = +4.43). On the null
(both effects switched off) across 8 seeds it recovers parent *t* mean +0.16 and
child *t* mean +0.36, with **|*t*| ≥ 2 in 0/8 seeds on both legs**. The windows, the
one-session lag and the calendar alignment are unbiased — the real-tape result is a
property of spin-offs, not of the harness.

## Verdict

- **Signal — Real (with the sign inverted), and only just.** One of the five pre-specified
  legs clears the desk's bar: the child under-performs SPY by **−4.54%** gross over its
  first **5** regular-way sessions (*t* = −2.73, HAC *t* = −3.02, bootstrap CI
  [−7.67, −1.42]% clear of zero, 8/26 positive; −4.77% net of a long position's frictions).
  It survives an era cut (both halves negative), a benchmark swap to IWM and MDY, a
  jackknife, de-clustering, and every cost setting, with |*t*| ≥ 2.2 on every one of those
  cuts. What it does **not** do is support the folklore it was built to test: Greenblatt's
  forced-seller story predicts the child is *cheap* and snaps back in the first days — the
  tape says it keeps falling for three sessions and only claws most of it back by the end
  of the month. The parent run-up (−1.45%, *t* = −0.26) and the sum-of-the-parts pop
  (+1.88%, *t* = +1.28) are **both null**. Three things keep this off any pedestal: the
  **family-wise *p* is 0.045**, i.e. real at 5% after paying for all five looks and no
  better than that; *survivorship is named twice over* (the table is curated to liquid,
  widely covered spins, and four events were lost because their child was acquired and
  delisted); and with n = 26, ~2 events a year and 8.5 pp of per-trade dispersion, the whole
  result rests on a small, hand-assembled sample whose single load-bearing input is a
  hand-compiled date.
- **Tradability — Fragile.** The alpha is negative, so the only way to bank it is to **short
  a freshly distributed spin-off for five sessions**: +4.32% per trade gross of borrow
  (*t* = +2.60), still +3.33% at a 50%/yr borrow, but only **+2.33% with a CI through zero**
  at 100%/yr — and a spin-off child in its first week is precisely the name where borrow is
  expensive, rationed or simply unavailable at any price, which the tape cannot tell us.
  Capacity is ~2 trades a year with an 8.5 pp per-trade standard deviation, and the window
  is so narrow that anchoring three sessions late turns +4.3% into −2.2%. Real effect,
  genuinely awkward trade.
